author: TeIq
content:
**Scope.** design.md §6 + §9. Every action (and key rotation, and config change) appends to an audit log; each row commits the SHA-256 hash of the previous row, making internal tampering detectable. Periodic external attestation of the head hash (object storage with object lock).

**Deliverables.**
- Migration: `audit_log (seq BIGSERIAL, ts, actor, kind, payload JSONB, prev_hash BYTEA, this_hash BYTEA)`.
- Insert trigger (or app-side enforcement) computes `this_hash = SHA256(prev_hash || canonical(payload) || ts || actor || kind)`.
- `polaris-backend/src/audit/`: `AuditLog` service + `record(event)` API used by every mutating path.
- Periodic head-hash attestation: a worker writes the current head hash to an S3 object-locked bucket every N minutes; an external auditor can compare local head against attested head.
- `cargo xtask audit-verify` reads the local audit log and asserts hash-chain integrity end-to-end.

**References.**
- design.md §6 (audit log append-only with hash chaining), §9 (insider tampering with audit log — mitigations).
- `.crosslink/rules/rigor.md` §Cryptographic correctness.

**Rust-quality.**
- Canonical-payload encoding is documented and version-pinned (CBOR with deterministic map ordering, via `proto-blue-lex-cbor`).
- SHA-256 via `sha2` crate (`.crosslink/rules/rust.md`).
- The hash chain is verified at app start in dev mode (fast); production runs it on a slower cadence + on demand.
- `unsafe` is not used anywhere in this subsystem.
- Object-lock S3 client never deletes; the attestation worker only PUTs new heads.

**Testing.**
- Tamper test: flip a byte in any row; `audit-verify` fails with a precise byte-offset diagnostic.
- Long-chain test: 100k events chain cleanly; `audit-verify` runs in < N seconds.
- Attestation round-trip: head hash written to S3 matches local head.

**Done when.** Audit chain is verifiable end-to-end; external attestation is observable in S3; the threat in §9 ("insider tampering with audit log") has a documented detection path.
